WITH RECURSIVE ancestry AS (
  -- Start from all classes that directly subclass ApiModel
  SELECT
    c.class_symbol_id,
    1 AS depth
  FROM code.class_bases c
  WHERE c.base_name = 'ApiModel'
  UNION ALL
  -- Recursively add intermediate classes
  SELECT
    c.class_symbol_id,
    a.depth + 1
  FROM code.class_bases c
  JOIN ancestry a ON c.ancestor_symbol_id = a.class_symbol_id
  WHERE c.base_name != 'ApiModel'  -- exclude ApiModel itself
),
final_chain AS (
  SELECT
    class_symbol_id,
    MAX(depth) AS depth
  FROM ancestry
  GROUP BY class_symbol_id
)
SELECT
  class_symbol_id,
  depth
FROM final_chain
WHERE depth > 1
ORDER BY depth, class_symbol_id;

request:
Which classes inherit from ApiModel (auto_ontology/server/models.py) only indirectly, i.e. through at least one intermediate class of this repository, and do not name ApiModel directly in their class statement? An import alias of ApiModel (auto_ontology/server/responses.py imports it as _Payload) counts as naming ApiModel directly, and a subscripted base such as ListResponse[T] counts as its class. For each, give the class symbol ID and the length of the shortest inheritance chain to ApiModel (2 when the parent class directly subclasses ApiModel).

Requested output columns: class_symbol_id (string), depth (integer).
explanation: The corrected query fixes the self-join condition in the recursive CTE. It now joins class_bases ancestry rows back to class_bases on the class_symbol_id, properly tracking the inheritance chain depth. The WHERE clause filters out direct ApiModel subclasses, leaving only classes with indirect inheritance.
sql:
WITH RECURSIVE ancestry AS (
  -- Start from all classes that directly subclass ApiModel
  SELECT
    c.class_symbol_id,
    1 AS depth
  FROM code.class_bases c
  WHERE c.base_name = 'ApiModel'
  UNION ALL
  -- Recursively add intermediate classes
  SELECT
    c.class_symbol_id,
    a.depth + 1
  FROM code.class_bases c
  JOIN ancestry a ON c.class_symbol_id = a.class_symbol_id
  WHERE c.base_name != 'ApiModel'
),
final_chain AS (
  SELECT
    class_symbol_id,
    MAX(depth) AS depth
  FROM ancestry
  GROUP BY class_symbol_id
)
SELECT
  class_symbol_id,
  depth
FROM final_chain
WHERE depth > 1
ORDER BY depth, class_symbol_id;
